newsitem.title: SWEDEN: INCENTIVE SAYS COMPETITION HIT MARGINS.
newsitem.headline: INCENTIVE SAYS COMPETITION HIT MARGINS.

text.p: Swedish investment company Incentive AB said on Monday price pressure within dialysis products depressed operating margins for Gambro, the group's key medical technology unit.
"In part the new clinics have not really started going and in part we are seeing some price pressure on dialysis products, above all in Europe," Incentive spokesman Bengt Modeer told Reuters.
Incentive recently bought Vivra, a U.S. dialysis clinic with around 270 clinics and 16,000 patients.
A weaker crown has had a small effect on the group's result, Modeer said.

Gambro posted a six-month operating profit of 776 million crowns, up from 709 million crowns for comparable units in the first half of 1996, while the operating margin fell to 12.2 percent from 13.2 percent.
Incentive posted an operating margin of 114 percent compared to 15.1 percent and an operating profit of 11.74 billion crowns after financial items compared to 1.99 billion crowns.
The increase was mostly due to a one-off gain of 11.10 billion crowns compared to 670 million, mostly from the sale of half its stake in electrical engineering group ABB AB for 12.4 billion crowns.
